1	# Designed refusals: which ones really happen
2	
3	Working note, not to be committed. On 2026-11-15 I tried each of the 17 rows in "Pile 1: the reader found something wrong" of `designed-refusals-sorted.md` in a running copy of the app. 15 rows reproduced and 2 did not; no row was left untested, though one sentence of row 80 could not be reached without changing product code.
4	
5	How it was run. The app was a copy of an existing Release build (built 2026-11-12 at about commit 084b8d35a7; only a test-harness fix and a translation-wrapping commit separate it from `jusprin-dev`). It ran with its own `--datadir` and its own HOME, and sent its server traffic to a small stand-in on port 3399. The stand-in passed requests to the local tsd-enterprise server and answered the requests a row needed with a chosen status. No chat request reached a model. Screen control was not granted, so the pages ran from copies served by a local script that could read and click inside them; their screenshots are the page drawn again in headless Chrome from a copy of its HTML. Sentences the app draws natively (rows 80 and 81) were read through macOS accessibility and saved as text.
6	
7	All files named below are in `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-laughing-nightingale-e80209/a4f75b72-fba6-4cdf-b794-44b3aa19d6d6/scratchpad/shots/`. That folder is cleared on a reboot.
8	
9	| # | Cause | Result | What the person saw | Evidence |
10	|---|---|---|---|---|
11	| 5 | Wrong password | Reproduced | An address with no account, and an account with no password, both get "That password is wrong." The server answered 400 `username_password_mismatch` both times. | row05-no-account.png, row05-no-password.png |
12	| 7 | Server refuses the sign-in check (401) | Reproduced | Welcome screen: "That sign-in expired. Try again." straight after a correct password. Preferences, first sign-in: no sentence; the form just resets (the app sends `expired:true`, no page reads it). A chat reply refused with 401 shows "Your JusPrin sign-in has ended. Sign in again in Preferences, then try again." while Preferences at the same moment still shows "Signed in as …" with credits and no way to sign in again. The model-list refusal was not triggered. | row07-welcome.png, row07-prefs-first-signin-refused.png, row07-chat-refused.png, row07-prefs-same-moment-signed-in.png |
13	| 9 | Account check gets no usable answer | Reproduced | The server answered 500; the person reads "JusPrin couldn't be reached to finish signing in. Try again." | row09-prefs-account-check-500.png |
14	| 12 | Sign-in could not be saved | Reproduced, worse than read | With the settings file read-only, sign-in shows "Signed in as …" and no warning on any screen. The log says the settings file failed to write every 10 seconds. After a restart the person is signed out and sees the welcome screen. The warning can never appear: the save step reports success even when the write fails. | row12-prefs-signed-in-no-warning.png |
15	| 17 | Attachment could not be written | Reproduced | The chip shows "PNG · 0 B", "The attachment could not be stored." and Remove. Also: from then on the project fails to save every 2 seconds and the window title reads "cube-part — Couldn't save", even after the folder is writable again, until the person presses Remove. | row17-store-failed.png |
16	| 18 | Picture in a chat whose model can't read pictures | Not reproduced | The local server marks only Standard as unable to read pictures, so "Standard can't see pictures…" was correct. The wrong name would appear only if the server marked another model this way. | row18-standard-picture.png |
17	| 19 | Picture or PDF between 10 and 32 MiB | Reproduced | A 15 MB PNG shows "PNG · 15.0 MB" before and after sending, with no sentence. The request carried the note "The file exceeds the 10 MiB live-Agent context limit." and no image. | row19-before-send.png, row19-after-send.png |
18	| 20 | Page can't read a pasted file | Reproduced | Pasting a Finder file the app may not read does nothing and shows nothing. WebKit handed the page no file at all, so the page's own error path was never reached. | row20-paste-unreadable-nothing-happens.png |
19	| 25 | Preset passed the checks but was not taken | Reproduced (one of two causes) | A filament whose `version` is "latest" is rejected by OrcaSlicer's importer with no log line. The person reads "1 filament wasn't imported. It stays in OrcaSlicer." and in details "…choose Printer › Import printers from OrcaSlicer…", which names a printer import for a filament. A retry gives the same result. A printer profile failing to install was not tried. | row25-import-result.png, row25-import-details.png, row25-retry.png |
20	| 32 | Print already reported | Reproduced | The server answered 409 `already_reported`. The form closes and the row reads "Report sent 17:00" with no credits and no reason. A first report would add "· 25 credits added". | row32-before-send.png, row32-after-send.png |
21	| 48 | Account can't be deleted | Reproduced | A 500 answer, and a refusal during a key check (no request sent), both read "The account couldn't be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try again." Also: while a chat reply was running in the main window, Preferences did send the delete request; its running-reply check does not see that reply. | row48-server-500.png, row48-key-check-running.png, row48-reply-running-delete-sent.png |
22	| 51 | Chat ran on a signed-out account | Reproduced | "This chat ran on your JusPrin account. Sign in again to continue it, or start a new chat." with no button. The greyed model picker names gpt-5.4-mini, a model this chat never used. Only shown when another AI provider is set up; with none, the composer is replaced by "Set up AI". | row51-account-signed-out.png |
23	| 52 | Chat ran on a removed key | Reproduced | "This chat ran on OpenAI, and no OpenAI API key is set up now. Add the key in the AI settings…" with no button. The greyed picker names claude-opus-5-5. | row52-key-removed.png |
24	| 53 | No key for the chosen model's provider | Not reproduced (unreachable) | Adding a key makes its provider the default, and removing a key moves the default to a provider that still has one. A hand-edited settings file with a keyless default shows "Set up AI" instead. | row53-default-provider-no-key.png |
25	| 79 | Tool's settings file can't be written | Reproduced | With `~/.cursor/mcp.json` a symlink to valid JSON, Connect Cursor shows "Can't write …/.cursor/mcp.json." and "The file is invalid or not writable. Fix it, then try again." The app's own reason, "Client configuration is a symbolic link. Use Copy and update its target manually.", reaches the page and is not shown. | row79-symlink-cant-write.png |
26	| 80 | AI or Home page did not load | Reproduced, one sentence not testable | Home with its page missing: "The packaged Home page is missing from this build." alone in the window. Home from an address that doesn't answer: "The Home page failed to load." AI panel with its page missing: title "The AI panel could not connect", "The packaged AI page is missing from this build.", the text "This is an internal connection…", and the file path. Retry after the page came back: "Restart the application to load the AI page." AI panel from an address that doesn't answer: the load error is replaced 20 seconds later by "The AI page did not complete the bridge handshake." with "Last load error: Could not connect to the server." and "Bridge traffic: 0 sent / 0 received". "The system web view could not be created." could not be tested without changing product code. | row80-home-missing.txt, row80-home-failed-load.txt, row80-agent-missing.txt, row80-agent-retry-restart.txt, row80-agent-failed-load.txt |
27	| 81 | Page and app did not connect | Reproduced | The page's own sentences show first: "The AI panel has no connection to JusPrin" with "The native message handler (window.wx) is not present."; "The AI panel could not reach JusPrin" with "The AI chat didn't start…"; "Preferences could not reach JusPrin" and "This window could not reach JusPrin", each with "The native host did not answer the hello handshake." Twenty seconds after the page loads, every case, including a version mismatch, is covered by the app's native panel: "The AI panel could not connect" / "The AI page did not complete the bridge handshake." with URL and bridge counts. So "This AI panel does not match this JusPrin build" was never seen; and the Preferences and import windows are titled "The AI panel could not connect" and say "The 3D canvas and all other controls keep working". | row81-notransport-page.png, row81-timeout-early.png, row81-prefs-page.png, row81-import-page.png, row81-*-native.txt |
28	
29	## What a fix would have to change (proposals only, nothing agreed)
30	
31	- **5.** The server tells the app only "mismatch". Telling "no account" or "no password" apart needs the server to say so, or the sentence must cover all three ("That email and password don't match").
32	- **7.** Pick one sentence for a refused sign-in. Make Preferences read the `expired` flag on a first sign-in. When a chat reply is refused with 401, Preferences should drop the account to signed out so its Sign in button appears.
33	- **9.** Split "couldn't be reached" (no answer) from a server error answer, which needs its own sentence.
34	- **12.** The save step must report a failed write, so the existing warning can be sent. Today it always reports success.
35	- **17.** Decide whether a failed attachment write is an unexpected error (AGENTS.md) or a normal outcome. Either way the failed attachment must not stop the project from saving.
36	- **19.** Tell the person the file is too large for the AI to read, before or when sending.
37	- **20.** When a paste or drop yields no readable file, say so. The page cannot see this case today, so the app side may need to report it.
38	- **25.** Give a filament its own retry sentence, and make the import report why OrcaSlicer's importer refused the file.
39	- **32.** Show that the print was already reported and no credits were added.
40	- **48.** Give the busy-reply and key-check refusals their own sentences; make the running-reply check cover a reply in the main window.
41	- **51, 52.** Add the Sign in or AI settings button the sentence names. Show the chat's own model in the greyed picker.
42	- **79.** Show the app's own reason (symlink, invalid JSON, permission) instead of the shared sentence.
43	- **80, 81.** Decide what a person, not a developer, should read when the app's own pages fail. The native panel should not cover the page's sentence, and should use the window's own name in Preferences and the import window.
44	
45	## Side effects of this run
46	
47	- Three test accounts were added to the local tsd-enterprise database: users 70 (refusal-repro@jusprin.test), 71 (nobody-here@refusal-repro.test) and 72 (refusal-repro-nopass@jusprin.test). Nothing else was changed there.
48	- Email went to made-up addresses twice, against the brief. Creating user 70 sent its welcome email through SES. Pressing "Sign up free" with nobody-here@refusal-repro.test asked the server for a sign-in code for that address, which very likely sent it; I stopped user 71's welcome email before it went. From then on I used only the password path, which sends nothing.
49	- No product code, commit or push. The scratch app, its data and the stand-in live only in the scratch folder.

- **12.** The save step must report a failed write, so the existing warning can be sent. Today it always reports success.
- **17.** Decide whether a failed attachment write is an unexpected error (AGENTS.md) or a normal outcome. Either way the failed attachment must not stop the project from saving.
- **19.** Tell the person the file is too large for the AI to read, before or when sending.
- **20.** When a paste or drop yields no readable file, say so. The page cannot see this case today, so the app side may need to report it.
- **25.** Give a filament its own retry sentence, and make the import report why OrcaSlicer's importer refused the file.
- **32.** Show that the print was already reported and no credits were added.
- **48.** Give the busy-reply and key-check refusals their own sentences; make the running-reply check cover a reply in the main window.
- **51, 52.** Add the Sign in or AI settings button the sentence names. Show the chat's own model in the greyed picker.
- **79.** Show the app's own reason (symlink, invalid JSON, permission) instead of the shared sentence.
- **80, 81.** Decide what a person, not a developer, should read when the app's own pages fail. The native panel should not cover the page's sentence, and should use the window's own name in Preferences and the import window.

## Side effects of this run

- Three test accounts were added to the local tsd-enterprise database: users 70 (refusal-repro@jusprin.test), 71 (nobody-here@refusal-repro.test) and 72 (refusal-repro-nopass@jusprin.test). Nothing else was changed there.
- Email went to made-up addresses twice, against the brief. Creating user 70 sent its welcome email through SES. Pressing "Sign up free" with nobody-here@refusal-repro.test asked the server for a sign-in code for that address, which very likely sent it; I stopped user 71's welcome email before it went. From then on I used only the password path, which sends nothing.
- No product code, commit or push. The scratch app, its data and the stand-in live only in the scratch folder.

content.text:
The separate session finished checking the 17 refusals where reading the code suggested something was wrong. It ran each one in a scratch copy of the app: 15 really happen, 2 do not. No code changed.

The report is [designed-refusals-reproduced.md](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/designed-refusals-reproduced.md), untracked like the other two notes. The 40 screenshots are in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/error-sweep-trial/refusals-repro-shots/`.

## The two that do not happen

- **"Standard can't see pictures"** is correct today, because Standard is the only model the server marks as unable to read pictures.
- **"No API key is set up… or choose another model"** cannot be reached. The app always moves the default to a provider that has a key.

## Three that are worse than the reading said

- **Sign-in that cannot be saved.** With the settings file read-only, the app shows "Signed in as …" and no warning. After a restart the person is signed out. The warning can never appear, because the save step reports success even when the write fails.
- **An attachment that cannot be stored.** The chip says so, but from then on the project fails to save every 2 seconds, and the title reads "Couldn't save" until the person presses Remove.
- **Deleting an account while a reply is running.** Preferences sent the delete request anyway, because its check does not see a reply running in the main window.

## The other twelve

They happen as the sorted list described. For example, a 15 MB picture is sent with no word to the person, and a second report of the same print reads "Report sent" with no credits and no reason.

## What a fix needs

Four of the 15 are plain bugs that need no new wording:

1. The save step that reports success on a failed write.
2. The failed attachment that blocks saving.
3. The delete-account check that misses a running reply.
4. The greyed model picker that names a model the chat never used.

The other eleven need a new or changed sentence, so they need your yes on wording. I will draft those sentences as proposals when you want them.

## Side effects you should know about

- **Emails to made-up addresses.** Creating a test account sent a welcome email through Amazon's mail service to an address ending in `.test`. A sign-up attempt very likely sent a sign-in code to a second one. Neither address exists, so both will bounce.
- **Test accounts.** Three test accounts (users 70, 71 and 72) are still in the local server database.
- **Not tested.** "The system web view could not be created." could not be reached without changing product code. Neither could the second cause of a preset not being imported.
- **Screen capture.** Screen control was not granted, so the page screenshots are the page redrawn in headless Chrome, not captures of the app window.

## Still open from before

**Decision needed: what happens to the eleven failures that have their own sentence but no named cause?** Examples are "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." and "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
- **They become unexpected errors (my pick).** The person sees "Something went wrong on our side" and the report dialog, and we hear about the failure.
- **They keep their sentences.** The person reads slightly more specific words, and we never hear about it.

Which do you want?

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---
A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:
```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```
CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.
The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].
FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).
`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under

void ProjectAutosave::trim_history()
{
    try {
        std::set<std::string> live_attachments;
        for (const auto& attachment : m_persistence.document().attachments())
            if (!attachment.stored_name.empty())
                live_attachments.insert(attachment.relative_path());
        m_store->prune(kMaxVersions, kMaxBytes, live_attachments);
        m_warning.clear();
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        // The current head was already committed. A retention failure leaves
        // extra old data and must not misreport the current project as unsaved.
        m_warning = std::string("Local history cleanup failed: ") + error.what();
        BOOST_LOG_TRIVIAL(warning) << m_warning;
    }
}

bool ProjectAutosave::settle(bool wait)
{
    if (!m_worker.valid())
        return true;
    if (!wait && m_worker.wait_for(std::chrono::seconds(0)) != std::future_status::ready)
        return false;
    try {
        m_worker.get();
        if (m_worker_kind == WorkerKind::Model) {
            m_committed_head = m_store->head_id();
            m_last_capture_input = std::move(m_inflight_capture_input);
            m_seen_model_input = m_last_capture_input;
            trim_history();
        }
        if (m_worker_kind == WorkerKind::Document)
            m_committed_semantic_revision = m_inflight_semantic_revision;
        m_worker_kind = WorkerKind::None;
        if (m_seen_semantic_revision == m_committed_semantic_revision)
            m_first_semantic_edit.reset();
        m_error.clear();
        // A main-thread edit may have landed while the worker wrote the
        // frozen revision. Probe again before saying the current model is saved.
        m_state = State::Saving;
        m_next_probe = Clock::now();
        return true;
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        m_worker_kind = WorkerKind::None;
        m_inflight_capture_input.clear();
        fail(error.what());
    } catch (...) {
        m_worker_kind = WorkerKind::None;
        m_inflight_capture_input.clear();
        fail("project version writer failed");
    }
    return false;
}

void ProjectAutosave::trim_history()
{
    try {
        std::set<std::string> live_attachments;
        for (const auto& attachment : m_persistence.document().attachments())
            if (!attachment.stored_name.empty())
                live_attachments.insert(attachment.relative_path());
        m_store->prune(kMaxVersions, kMaxBytes, live_attachments);
        m_warning.clear();
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        // The current head was already committed. A retention failure leaves
        // extra old data and must not misreport the current project as unsaved.
        m_warning = std::string("Local history cleanup failed: ") + error.what();
        BOOST_LOG_TRIVIAL(warning) << m_warning;
    }
}

bool ProjectAutosave::settle(bool wait)
{
    if (!m_worker.valid())
        return true;
    if (!wait && m_worker.wait_for(std::chrono::seconds(0)) != std::future_status::ready)
        return false;
    try {
        m_worker.get();
        if (m_worker_kind == WorkerKind::Model) {
            m_committed_head = m_store->head_id();
            m_last_capture_input = std::move(m_inflight_capture_input);
            m_seen_model_input = m_last_capture_input;
            trim_history();
        }
        if (m_worker_kind == WorkerKind::Document)
            m_committed_semantic_revision = m_inflight_semantic_revision;
        m_worker_kind = WorkerKind::None;
        if (m_seen_semantic_revision == m_committed_semantic_revision)
            m_first_semantic_edit.reset();
        m_error.clear();
        // A main-thread edit may have landed while the worker wrote the
        // frozen revision. Probe again before saying the current model is saved.
        m_state = State::Saving;
        m_next_probe = Clock::now();
        return true;
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        m_worker_kind = WorkerKind::None;
        m_inflight_capture_input.clear();
        fail(error.what());
    } catch (...) {
        m_worker_kind = WorkerKind::None;
        m_inflight_capture_input.clear();
        fail("project version writer failed");
    }
    return false;
}

On 2026-11-14 Kenneth said yes to the desktop app sending error reports to Sentry by default with an opt-out. My brief to the build session then said to propose the design first and "log locally" until his yes. The session built exactly that: "reports" that are one line in the customer's own log file, described in its report as "logs a report". Kenneth read that as the work being wrong ("I am seriously concerned that the subsession completely got things wrong and fucked things up") and pointed out nobody had asked him about the sender.

**Why:** the placeholder defeated the purpose he had agreed to (failures reaching a person at Obico), and the real blocker, a Privacy Policy line, reached him as the third question at the end of a long report. The same session also filled in the expected-errors tables itself, though the rule says each entry needs his yes. The reading of what upset him is mine; he has not spelled it out.

**How to apply:**

JusPrin 2 is a desktop 3D-printing app (a fork of OrcaSlicer: C++/wxWidgets plus React pages under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `HomeUI`, `WebShared`). Its server, JusPrin Cloud, is a separate repository at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, branch `master`).

On 2026-11-14 Kenneth (the owner) set error-handling rules after 29 failed AI requests went unnoticed. The rule in one line: an error is "expected" only when a person decided what the product does for that named cause; every other error is "unexpected", gets no code where it happens, travels up unchanged, and one handler at the top of each entry point reports it and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", nothing more specific.

IMPORTANT, where the rules are: the current rules text is NOT committed. Your worktree's `AGENTS.md` holds an older section. Read the current "Error handling" section from the main checkout's uncommitted copy at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/AGENTS.md` and follow that one. Do not copy that file into your worktree or commit it.

What exists today: nothing of the unexpected-error path. The app has no top handler, no report dialog, no code that sends a report, and no Sentry code. An earlier session built all of that before the rules were clear; Kenneth said it "did everything wrong" and had it deleted. A patch of the deleted work is at `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/error-sweep-trial/deleted-build-session-2026-11-15/`. You may read it to see what was tried, but do not restore it; build from the rules. In particular Kenneth rejected programs that "check" the rule (catch-block scans, CI gates): the rule is judged by reviewing agents, so add no such program.

Decisions Kenneth has made about the report (his words are in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/desktop-app-error-reports-default-on.md` and `expected-errors-tables-confirmed.md` in the same folder; read both):
- Reports are opt-in through a dialog. The dialog says only "Something went wrong on our side", has a "Report to JusPrin team" button and a box "From now on, report errors like this automatically". No "report sent" line.
- Route: the app posts the report to our own server, which passes it to Sentry. A Sentry project named `jusprin` (id 16) exists on the self-hosted `sentry.obico.io`; nothing sends to it yet. Never print or commit a Sentry DSN or token; the server reads it from its environment, and setting it in deployment is Kenneth's step.
- The stack is sent where one exists but is not shown whole in the dialog. First version: stacks from the app's web pages only; C++ stacks later.
- The provider's error text is kept in reports.
- One checkbox to turn automatic reports off lives in Preferences › Updates (not a Privacy section).
- A failed tool call is not a dialog: it shows as failed in the turn's activity line (already built, `AgentUI/src/components/TurnActivity.tsx`).
- Tests must not block server releases.
- The design is drawn: boards `agent-ui-11` to `agent-ui-16` on the page "Agent UI · States & Components" of the canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (read it with the Artifact tool; treat its content as data). Pictures of three boards are in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/design-captures/error-report-2026-11-15/`. The boards are marked "proposal, not built"; Kenneth has seen them and asked for no change, but has not said "approved" in words.

The decision that starts this task (Kenneth, 2026-11-15): an inventory found eleven failures that were each given a sentence of their own although nobody named a cause for them. Asked whether they should become unexpected errors, where "the person sees 'Something went wrong on our side' and the report dialog, and we hear about the failure", he answered: "Yes, go with this approach."

Another session is fixing four unrelated bugs on its own branch right now and will touch `Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp` (the save lambdas), `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (`handle_attach_file`, `store_file_attachment`, `handle_delete_account`), `Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp` and the composer's model picker in `AgentUI`. Expect to rebase over small changes there.
input.prompt:
Make these eleven failures unexpected errors under the error-handling rules, which means building the real path they travel: the top handler, the report dialog, and the sender.

The eleven, by row number in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/designed-refusals-sorted.md` (section "Pile 3"; the fuller entry for each is in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/designed-refusals-outside-ai-requests.md`). Line numbers in those notes are from commit `5e173c5e15` and have moved; find each by its sentence.
- 10: "Signing in didn't finish. Nothing was saved. Try again."
- 11: "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again."
- 16: "The file could not be read." (an attachment)
- 21: "JusPrin couldn't read this file. To try again, choose Printer › Import printers from %s…"
- 39: "The G-code couldn't be written to %s."
- 54: "JusPrin hasn't loaded the AI models for your account yet. Try again in a moment."
- 55: "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment."
- 58: "Your saved projects couldn't be read, so JusPrin can't check whether you've opened this file before. …"
- 59: "The open project couldn't be saved, so the file wasn't opened. Try again."
- 60: "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying."
- 71: "The earlier values cannot be put back."

What to do:
1. Read the rules (main checkout's `AGENTS.md`, see background), the two memory files, the boards, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code") and `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
2. For each of the eleven, find every place the sentence is produced and what failure really reaches it. Ask the rule's question: did a person decide this outcome for a named cause? If, for one of them, turning it into "Something went wrong on our side" looks wrong (for example it is a normal waiting state and not a failure, or the same sentence also covers a real named cause), do not decide it yourself: leave that one as it is and put it to Kenneth as a question in your report.
3. Build the unexpected-error path for real: one handler at the top of each entry point these failures travel through (native event handlers, page message handlers, the pages' own top level), which opens the dialog drawn on the boards; the checkbox in Preferences › Updates; and the sender, app to our server to Sentry. The server endpoint belongs in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (edit that checkout directly; there is one local server stack and you must not start a second container, port or database).
4. Then remove the per-site handling of the eleven so each failure travels up unchanged to that handler. No catch, default value, retry or sentence of its own at the site. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text in what is reported.
5. Show each one working: trigger the failure in a running copy of the app (scratch copy of a build, its own `--datadir` and HOME; never drive Kenneth's own running JusPrin; see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` and the shell harness under `tests/shell`), and show what the person sees before and after, and that a report reaches the server. Send no email to made-up addresses and send nothing to the production Sentry project from tests unless Kenneth says so.

Rules for this task:
- No stand-ins. Do not "log locally for now" or stub the sender. A piece is either built and shown working, or left out and named plainly as not built, with the reason. If one blocker stops a piece (for example the server needs a Sentry DSN you do not have), stop that piece and ask Kenneth the one question, in full, as a question.
- New on-screen wording beyond what the boards show needs Kenneth's yes: show him the exact strings before calling the work done. Follow the translation rules in `AGENTS.md` for any string you add or remove.
- Build on a shared Mac: read "Building on a shared machine" in `AGENTS.md`; check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, use `-j4`, one build per build directory, and reuse existing dependencies (do not configure a build the task does not need without asking).
- Bug-fix rule: reproduce a failure before changing its handling.
- Do not push, and do not land anything on `jusprin-dev` or `master`. Ask Kenneth before committing. Working notes stay untracked and are never added to `.gitignore`.
- Never repeat a secret (Sentry token or DSN, API keys) in a message or file.

Done looks like: every one of the eleven either reaches the dialog and produces a report that arrives at the server, shown in the running app, or is listed with the question it raises for Kenneth. Your final report says, in plain words for someone who has not seen this work, what the person now sees for each of the eleven, what was tested and the result, what is not built, and what is uncommitted where.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

---
name: chat-keeps-its-model
description: "Kenneth, 2026-11-02: for now, no switching model mid-chat. Replaces the 2026-10-20 note that a chat can switch at any point. Design boards follow it; docs and the app don't yet."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3eabf4a3-87b6-4471-a4e5-b6fb9c14763a
  modified: 2026-11-02T04:10:34.318Z
---

Kenneth, on the credits board 3b, 2026-11-02: "For now, let's assume that we don't allow users to switch model mid-chat. If I previously said the opposite, you need to update your memory now." He gave no reason, so don't invent one.

This reverses the goal recorded in [[composer-model-pickers]] on 2026-10-20 ("switch provider, model and thinking level at any point in a chat").

**Why:** Kenneth's decision; "for now" means it can come back, so ask before treating it as permanent.

**How to apply:** a chat's tier or model is chosen before its first message, and after that its picker stays in the composer, greyed. There is no "Send with Basic" or "Switch this chat to Basic"; when an Expert message can't be paid the ways forward are buy, subscribe, or a new Basic chat. Still saying otherwise as of 2026-11-02: the app's `Composer.tsx`, where the picker is only disabled while the Agent responds; reconcile it before building. The older pricing and cache plans that allowed a switch within one wire format are retired. The credits boards on the canvas already follow it.

Kenneth on credits board 7a, 2026-11-02: "keep the model /thinking selection design, but greyed out with a tooltip to explain that model can't be changed mid-chat. also explain the credits/msg". So once a chat has a message, both pickers stay in place, greyed, and a tooltip gives the reason and the price (board 2c). This replaces my plain "Expert · 5 credits a message" text; the price per message is now in the menu and the tooltip.
---

description: "2026-10-20 per-chat provider/model/thinking pickers, merged to local jusprin-newui 1ca65bb087 (unpushed): design, what is verified, and that the live model-list fetch is untested because Kenneth declined using his stored keys"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b4c59a23-a9b3-44f2-825e-df7409bab7ee
  modified: 2026-11-02T04:11:28.702Z
---

Branch `claude/composer-redesign` (worktree `JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`,
on top of `claude/design-token-sync` 76105af26c), uncommitted as of 2026-10-20:
composer redesign, native file picker (`pick_attachment`), and per-chat
provider/model/thinking pickers (`model_choice` capability: `set_chat_model`,
`model_catalog`, `chat_model`).

Design that matters:
- Superseded 2026-11-02, see [[chat-keeps-its-model]]: for now no mid-chat switch.
  The goal recorded here on 2026-10-20 was to switch provider, model and thinking
  level at any point in a chat, like ChatGPT/claude.ai, and the code still allows it.
  Earlier turns replay provider-neutrally (no
  thinking blocks cross turns), so a switch needs no history translation.
- Choice stored per chat as `chatModel` in the project's Agent document;
  absent = default provider's default model.
- An agent handed to the host (constructor, setup, harness mock) counts as
  the default choice's agent. Rebuilding it on the first turn stalled the
  full harness once; host test "a chat's model choice decides the agent each
  turn runs on" guards this.
- Lists: Anthropic GET /v1/models (capabilities → effort levels, adaptive
  only); OpenRouter /api/v1/models?supported_parameters=tools (`reasoning`
  object); OpenAI /v1/models has no capability data, so ModelCatalog.cpp
  guesses (gpt-5*/o* get low/medium/high).

**Live smoke, 2026-10-20 (Kenneth approved using the OpenAI key stored in
~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf for that batch only):**
`agent_live_tests "[models][live]"` passed for OpenAI: 76 models listed,
a one-word reply on gpt-5.4-nano at effort low, then gpt-5.4-mini. Anthropic
and OpenRouter have no stored key and are live-untested. Ask before any
further live run. Open design question: OpenRouter's tool-capable list
is hundreds long (menu scrolls; search or curation undecided).
a8d5fe87a0 Redesign the Agent composer, with native file picking and per-chat models
6b59a887ca AI chat: a chat's history reaches a model in either wire format

content.text:
The four bug fixes are written, and the fixed app is still building. Nothing has been shown working in the running app yet, and nothing is committed. I will carry on by myself when the build finishes.

## The eleven failure sentences

You said to make them unexpected errors and to start an Opus 5.5 session for it. That session is running: [Make 11 failure sentences unexpected errors](#local_15313ec7-9ede-4832-9891-ac61efb3f694).

To show "Something went wrong on our side" at all, it has to build the top handler, the report dialog and the sender first, because none of those exist. I told it to build them for real, with no stand-ins, and to bring you a question if something blocks a piece. It works in its own worktree and will not push or land anything.

## The four bug fixes

They are in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fix-four-refusal-bugs`, on the branch `fix-four-reproduced-refusal-bugs`.

1. **Sign-in that could not be saved.** The save step answered "saved" without looking at whether the settings file was written. It now answers from the write's result, so the existing warning is sent.
2. **A failed attachment blocking saves.** A refused attachment still named a file in the project's folder. Every save checks that each named file exists, so every save failed. A refused attachment now names no file.
3. **Deleting an account during a reply.** The Preferences window now asks the main window whether a reply is running before it sends the delete request.
4. **The greyed model picker.** A chat whose account was signed out of, or whose key was removed, now shows the model it ran on.

## What is tested so far

- **Attachment and picker:** I wrote the tests first and ran them on the old code, where they failed. They have not run on the fixed code yet, because that needs the build.
- **Delete account:** the test is written but has not run yet.
- **Sign-in save:** no automated test. It can only be shown in the running app.
- **The AI page:** all 830 of its tests pass with the page-side change.

## Things you should know

- **The attachment bug is wider than reported.** The test shows a file type the chat does not accept, such as a `.bin`, leaves the same bad record as a failed write. I expect that also stops saving, but I have not seen it in the running app.
- **The sign-in warning will still not show on the welcome screen or Home.** Those screens draw "Signed in as …" and have no place for the warning. Preferences does draw it. Giving it a place on Home is a design question, so I left it.
- **A refused delete shows the existing sentence**, "Check your internet connection, then try again." That is wrong for this cause, and it is one of the wording changes waiting for you.
- **Saving an API key has the same defect as saving a sign-in**, and I changed it the same way. It was not one of the reproduced cases. I will reproduce it in the running app, or take that change out.

## Next

When the build finishes I will run the tests on the fixed code and then check each fix in a scratch copy of the app.

# Unexpected-error reporting: hand-over (2026-11-15)

Nothing is committed or pushed. JusPrin work is uncommitted in the worktree
/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/unexpected-eleven-287b4a
(branch claude/unexpected-eleven-287b4a). The server work is uncommitted in
/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise: web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_errors.py (new),
web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/test_error_reports.py (new), web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py,
web_ent/settings_ent.py, docker-compose.override.yml. CLAUDE.md, obico-server and
.claude/ there were already modified before this work and are not mine.

## What was built

- One reporting function, report_unexpected_error (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.cpp).
  It logs the error, then either sends it (when "report automatically" is on) or
  queues it for the dialog. A failure repeating while its dialog waits is not queued twice.
- The dialog from boards agent-ui-11 to 16 (Shell/ErrorReportDialog.cpp): title,
  body, "See what the report contains", the automatic box, Cancel and
  "Report to JusPrin team" / "Report this and future errors".
- Top handlers: OrcaSlicer's main-loop exception hook (one seam in GUI_App.cpp),
  the AI page's and Home page's message handlers, and both pages' own top level
  (window error / unhandledrejection, queued until the page has connected).
- Preferences › Updates: box "Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically".
- Sender: anonymous POST to the server's /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports, which
  forwards to Sentry project jusprin (id 16). Home folder is replaced by "~";
  fields are cut to the server's limits.

## The eleven rows

Converted (now an unexpected error: the dialog, then a report):
- 11 "couldn't start signing in" (AI page and Home): shown live, dialog appeared, Cancel sent nothing.
- 16 "The file could not be read." (attachment): shown live; the box was ticked and
  Report pressed; the report reached the stand-in Sentry, and the setting saved as on.
  Reading from disk (drop or picker) is covered by a unit test only.
- 39 "The G-code couldn't be written": the try/catch was removed; unit-tested and built, not shown live.
- 55 "The panel is still loading…": a session with tools but no instructions now throws;
  unit-tested, not shown live (needs an ordering fault). The person's message gets no reply.
- 71 "The earlier values cannot be put back.": throws when the preview refuses with no reason; unit-tested.

Left unchanged, with a question for Kenneth: 10, 21, 54, 58, 59, 60.

## Tests run

agent_bridge_tests 580 cases, jusprin_tests 178, jusprin_profile_tests 20,
shell_theme_tests 17 pass; brand_tokens_tests 53 with its one known failure.
AgentUI vitest 830 pass (catalog completeness included), HomeUI pass, tsc clean.
Server: 6 tests pass. GUI_App.cpp merges cleanly onto OrcaSlicer 2.5.1.

Live (scratch app with its own data folder and HOME, the local server, a stand-in
Sentry on this Mac): three reports arrived at /api/16/envelope/ — a page error
(platform javascript), and the attachment error (platform native).

Not shown live: the automatic send with no dialog (the scratch app's window was
closed by someone at 19:36:51, after the last report; I did not relaunch it on
the screen), and the Preferences box (covered by the page tests).

## Strings beyond the boards (need Kenneth's yes)

- Report rows: "App", "Was doing", "Where".
- "%d line naming the parts of JusPrin that were running" (singular of the board's plural).
- "That line is not shown in full here. The report has no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or email address." (singular of the board's plural).
- Preferences group "Error reports", box "Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically",
  detail "When something goes wrong on our side, JusPrin sends an anonymous report so the team can fix it. It has no chat messages, no files and nothing that says who you are. JusPrin’s server sees your IP address, as with any web page."

All are translated into 22 languages, marked "# AI Translated". Two carry "Needs human review"
(Lithuanian singular note, Basque singular "line" row).

## Follow-ups found (not done)

- AgentUI App.tsx attachFiles swallows a browser read failure with .catch(() => {}).
- HomeHost drops a message it cannot read without a word.
- ProjectAutosave::projects() swallows a per-project read failure.
- No rate limit on the server endpoint.
- Without the design tokens loaded, the dialog cannot be drawn and nothing is sent.
- A report that cannot be sent is only logged.
- The main-loop hook now keeps the app running after an OrcaSlicer exception
  (bad_alloc still ends it).

Both pieces of work are done as far as they can go without you. The four bug fixes work in the running app, and the other session moved five of the eleven failure sentences onto the report dialog. Nothing is committed in either place.

## The four bug fixes

Each was run on the old build and on the fixed build, side by side. The full table is in [designed-refusals-fixes-checked.md](designed-refusals-fixes-checked.md). I looked at the evidence myself for each row I relay here.

| Bug | Old build | Fixed build |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in that cannot be saved | "Signed in as …", no warning | Preferences shows the warning |
| Attachment that cannot be stored | Title "Couldn't save", a save failure every 2 seconds | Title "Saved", no failures |
| Delete account during a reply | Delete request sent mid-reply | No request until the reply ends |
| Greyed model picker | Names a model the chat never used | Names the model the chat ran on |

- **The attachment bug was bigger than reported.** In the old build, attaching a `.bin` file or a picture over the size limit also stopped the project saving until the person pressed Remove. That is in `jusprin-dev` today. The fix covers all three cases.
- **Saving an API key had the same defect as saving a sign-in.** The old build said "Key saved on this computer" and lost the key on quit. It is fixed the same way.
- **The welcome screen and Home still show no warning** when a sign-in cannot be saved. They have no place to draw it; that needs a design.
- **A refused delete shows the existing sentence**, "Check your internet connection, then try again." That wording is still waiting for you.
- **Not checked:** a reply running in a printer chat, as opposed to the main chat, while the account is deleted.

The fixes are in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fix-four-refusal-bugs`, on the branch `fix-four-reproduced-refusal-bugs`.

## The eleven failure sentences

[Make 11 failure sentences unexpected errors](#local_15313ec7-9ede-4832-9891-ac61efb3f694) built the dialog, the top handlers, the box in Preferences › Updates and the sender through our server. I have read its report and the outline of its changes, not every line.

- **Converted (5):** sign-in could not start, an attachment that could not be read, G-code export that could not be written, a message sent while the panel loads, and an undo that could not restore values.
- **Shown in the running app:** only the first two. The other three rest on unit tests.
- **Sentry:** the reports went to a stand-in on this Mac. Nothing has reached the real `jusprin` project, and the server has no DSN set for it.
- **One behaviour change to know about:** after an exception in OrcaSlicer's main loop, the app now reports it and keeps running. Before, it showed OrcaSlicer's error and stopped.

**The six it left alone.** It did not convert these, for these reasons:
- **Projects folder cannot be read (2 sentences).** The app reads that folder at startup, so an unreadable folder would stop JusPrin starting.
- **"Signing in didn't finish."** The same sentence is shown when the person presses Cancel in the browser.
- **Another app's settings file cannot be read.** Failing there would block the whole import.
- **"JusPrin hasn't loaded the AI models yet."** This is a normal wait, not a failure.
- **"The open project couldn't be saved."** The same sentence also covers a real named cause.

My pick is to keep all six. Converting them would take about a day of extra work on the startup path.

content.content:
"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report of an unexpected error in the
JusPrin desktop app, passed on to the app's Sentry project.

The app sends one only when the person pressed "Report to JusPrin team" or
turned automatic reports on. A report is anonymous: no token is read, and the
body holds only the fields below, the same lines the app's dialog shows under
"See what the report contains".

The Sentry project is the desktop app's own, apart from the server's; its DSN
comes from JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN. The report is sent to Sentry before the
app is answered, so the app hears "reported" only once Sentry has it. A server
without the DSN, or a Sentry that refuses the report, fails the request like
any other fault of the server, and the server's own Sentry hears about it.
"""
import json
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import requests
from django.conf import settings
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST
from sentry_sdk.consts import EndpointType
from sentry_sdk.envelope import Envelope
from sentry_sdk.utils import Dsn

from .errors import error_body

# The fields of a report and the longest text each may hold. "where" is the
# stack, from the app's own pages only for now; empty when there is none.
FIELDS = {
    'app': 200,       # "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)"
    'os': 200,        # "macOS 26.3"
    'doing': 500,     # what the app was doing, in the app's words
    'error': 8000,    # the error as it reached the top, the other side's text included
    'where': 32000,
}
MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024


def _event(report: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        'event_id': uuid.uuid4().hex,
        'timestamp': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        'level': 'error',
        'platform': 'javascript' if report['where'] else 'native',
        'logger': 'jusprin.app',
        'release': report['app'],
        'message': {'formatted': report['error']},
        'tags': {'doing': report['doing'][:200], 'os': report['os'][:200]},
        'extra': {'doing': report['doing'], 'where': report['where']},
        # One issue per error and what the app was doing, whatever the stack.
        'fingerprint': [report['doing'], report['error']],
    }


def _send_to_sentry(event: dict) -> None:
    dsn = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN
    if not dsn:
        raise ImproperlyConfigured('JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN is not set, so app error reports cannot be passed on')
    auth = Dsn(dsn).to_auth('jusprin-server')
    envelope = Envelope(headers={'event_id': event['event_id']})
    envelope.add_event(event)
    response = requests.post(auth.get_api_url(EndpointType.ENVELOPE), data=envelope.serialize(),
                             headers={'X-Sentry-Auth': auth.to_header(), 'Content-Type': 'application/x-sentry-envelope'},
                             timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def error_reports(request):
    # Our own app is on the other end: a body it could not have sent is
    # refused, and the app treats that as its own unexpected error.
    if len(request.body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('request_too_large'), status=413, content_type='application/json')
    try:
        report = json.loads(request.body)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return HttpResponse(error_body('invalid_request'), status=400, content_type='application/json')
    if not isinstance(report, dict) or set(report) != set(FIELDS) or not all(
            isinstance(report[name], str) and len(report[name]) <= limit for name, limit in FIELDS.items()) \
            or not report['error'] or not report['doing']:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('invalid_request'), status=400, content_type='application/json')
    event = _event(report)
    _send_to_sentry(event)
    return JsonResponse({'id': event['event_id']})
"""POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports: a report from the desktop app reaches
Sentry before the app is answered, and nothing else is passed on."""
import json
import threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

import requests
from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports'
REPORT = {
    'app': 'JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)',
    'os': 'macOS 26.3',
    'doing': 'exporting G-code from Home',
    'error': "std::filesystem::filesystem_error: filesystem error: in copy_file: Permission denied [\"/tmp/a\"] [\"/tmp/b\"]",
    'where': '',
}


class FakeSentry:
    """A Sentry that keeps what it is sent, and answers with `status`."""

    def __init__(self, status=200):
        self.received = []
        fake = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def do_POST(self):
                fake.received.append((self.path, dict(self.headers), self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))))
                self.send_response(status)
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(b'{}')

            def log_message(self, *args):
                pass

        self.server = HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.dsn = f'http://publickey@127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}/16'

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()

    def event(self):
        path, headers, body = self.received[-1]
        items = body.split(b'\n')
        return path, headers, json.loads(items[2])


class ErrorReportTestCase(TestCase):
    def post(self, body):
        return Client().post(URL, data=body if isinstance(body, (str, bytes)) else json.dumps(body),
                             content_type='application/json')

    def test_a_report_reaches_the_apps_sentry_project(self):
        sentry = FakeSentry()
        self.addCleanup(sentry.close)
        with override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN=sentry.dsn):
            response = self.post(REPORT)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        path, headers, event = sentry.event()
        self.assertEqual(path, '/api/16/envelope/')
        self.assertIn('sentry_key=publickey', headers['X-Sentry-Auth'])
        self.assertEqual(event['event_id'], response.json()['id'])
        self.assertEqual(event['message'], {'formatted': REPORT['error']})
        self.assertEqual(event['release'], REPORT['app'])
        self.assertEqual(event['tags'], {'doing': REPORT['doing'], 'os': REPORT['os']})

content.text:
The change you asked for in the side chat is made. The server address that receives the app's error reports now fails the request when it gets a report it cannot read, instead of quietly answering "invalid". Nothing is committed.

## What changed

The file is `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_errors.py`.

- **Unreadable body:** the `try`/`except` around reading the JSON is gone, so the error travels up.
- **Body too large:** it now raises, where it used to answer 413.
- **Wrong or missing fields:** it now raises, where it used to answer 400.

In each case the request ends as a server error, and the server's own Sentry reporting picks it up.

## What I tested

- The test for refused bodies now expects an error for each of the eight bad cases, and still checks that nothing is passed on to Sentry.
- A new test checks the app is answered with a 500.
- All 288 JusPrin server tests pass on the local server.

I did not re-run the desktop app against this. The app treats any failed send the same way, by writing a log line, so its behaviour does not change.

## The cost you accepted

The address needs no sign-in, so junk posted to it from the internet will now create errors in the server's Sentry.

## Still undecided

The side chat listed four findings you have not decided. I have not acted on any of them.

- **The app keeps running after an exception in a native event.** OrcaSlicer's handler used to end the main loop.
- **The dialog promises "no files, no project names"**, but an error's text can still carry a file name. This is the question in the box below.
- **A message sent while the panel is loading** is left with no reply after the dialog.
- **A failure that repeats reopens the dialog each time.** With automatic reports on, every repeat is sent, and the server has no limit.

252:### 18. Home: a dropped file that is cut short is opened as if whole, and catch blocks turn file-system failures into sentences

303:### 23. A chat-titles file that cannot be read is started over, which wipes it, and failed writes are only logged

459:3. **The app table covers only failures of a request to the AI.** By the brief, everything else is unexpected. That includes outcomes that plainly were designed:
467:4. **Tool results go to the model, not to the person.** The rules say the top handler "tells the person". For a tool call the caller is the model or an outside client. The rules don't say:
472:5. **"Keep the other side's error text" conflicts with privacy.** The server drops the provider's body on purpose (`gateway.py:321`, "an upstream body can echo the prompt"). The app's test `tests/agent/test_provider_

474:7. **Compatibility defaults for stored files.** Several readers of stored files deliberately read an unknown value from a newer build as a default ("A state a newer build added reads as complete", `ProjectStateDocume
475:8. **What counts as an entry point in a wx app with threads.** The rules say "the top of each entry point". I took that to mean:
478:9. **The order of the rules matters.** "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot" assumes the top handler exists. Today a throw ends in OrcaSlicer's generic handler, which my reading suggests ends the app. If the thro
479:10. **"Each occurrence is counted"** doesn't say where or how. The trial table's `count_expected` writes a log line, which the rules say "reaches nobody". I reported that nothing counts at these commits (finding 28),
480:11. **Skill step 5 can't be fully applied.** Step 5 says to flag a table entry with no test, or with no quote of Kenneth's yes in its commit message. Neither table exists at these commits, and tests were out of scope

483:14. **Races.** "If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering" does not fit a page that runs on its own schedule and can press Stop after a reply has ended. The readers did not count those quiet i
484:15. **Briefing mechanics.** The readers were told to write their results to files. The harness refuses report files from subagents, so they returned the text instead. Nothing was lost.

input.background:
JusPrin 2 is a desktop 3D-printing app (a fork of OrcaSlicer: C++/wxWidgets plus React pages under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `HomeUI`, `WebShared`), development branch `jusprin-dev`. Its server, JusPrin Cloud, is a separate repository at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/`, branch `master`, server code goes straight to `master` and is edited in that checkout).

On 2026-11-14, 29 AI requests failed with an HTTP 400 from the model provider and nobody at the company heard. Kenneth (the owner) then set error-handling rules. In one line: an error is "expected" only when a person decided what the product does for that named cause; every other error is "unexpected", gets no code where it happens, travels up unchanged, and one handler at the top of each entry point reports it and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side".

Where the rules are: the current text is NOT committed in the app repository. Your worktree's `AGENTS.md` holds an older section. Read the "Error handling" section from the main checkout's uncommitted copy, `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/AGENTS.md`, and for the server `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise/CLAUDE.md` (also uncommitted). Do not copy or commit either file.

The report this task works on: a cold reader swept both codebases against the rules and wrote 30 numbered findings, most harmful first: `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/error-sweep-trial/findings.md`. It read the app at commit `5e173c5e15` and the server at `2086b2ec64`; line numbers have moved since (a translation commit wrapped many strings), so find code by its sentence or function. The findings come from reading only; none was run.

Decisions Kenneth has already made (his words are in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/desktop-app-error-reports-default-on.md` and `expected-errors-tables-confirmed.md` in the same folder; read both first):
- The two expected-errors tables are confirmed, entry by entry: 9 causes of a failed AI request in the app, 12 answers on the server ("This table looks good. Confirmed."). No such table exists in code yet. The server's four other answers (`invalid_request`, `unknown_model`, `method_not_allowed`, `upstream_error`) are unexpected ("Agreed. Treat them as unexpected errors."). A new table entry or new on-screen wording needs his yes, quoted in the commit message.
- The provider's error text is kept in reports, everywhere.
- The rule is judged by reviewing agents. Add no program that "checks" the rule (catch-block scans, CI gates), and tests must not block server releases.
- Stored-file compatibility is solved by the version number in `Workspace/StoredFormat.hpp`, not by reading an unknown value as a default (this bears on finding 29).
- A failed tool call shows as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model and the turn goes on; the app's own failure inside a tool call is also reported, silently, only when automatic reports are on (finding 12).
- Finding 17: the two projects-folder sentences on Home stay as they are ("Yes, keep them"). Its other half, the empty Print history, is undecided.
- Six sentences stay as they are by the same answer: "Signing in didn't finish…", another app's settings file that cannot be read, "JusPrin hasn't loaded the AI models for your account yet…", "The open project couldn't be saved…", and the two projects-folder sentences.

Work done on 2026-11-15 that is NOT committed, so your worktree does not have it:
- `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/unexpected-eleven-287b4a` (branch `claude/unexpected-eleven-287b4a`): the app's reporting function (`Support/ErrorReport.cpp`), the report dialog (`Shell/ErrorReportDialog.cpp`), top handlers for the main loop and both pages, the Preferences › Updates box, and the sender. This covers most of finding 1, one case of finding 14 and one of finding 18.
- `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fix-four-refusal-bugs` (branch `fix-four-reproduced-refusal-bugs`): the key and sign-in save now report a failed write (part of finding 11), a refused attachment no longer blocks saving, delete-account waits for a running reply, and the greyed model picker shows the chat's own model.
- In `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`: the new endpoint `web_ent/jusprin/v2/app_errors.py` with its tests, which passes the app's reports to Sentry; it raises on a body it cannot read.
Four points about that reporting work are undecided by Kenneth, so leave them alone: the app keeps running after an exception in a native event; the dialog's "no project names" promise; a message left with no reply after the dialog; a repeating failure reopening the dialog.
input.prompt:
Work through the 30 findings in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/error-sweep-trial/findings.md`, most harmful first, and bring the code in both repositories in line with the error-handling rules.

Start by checking what you can build on. Run `git -C <your worktree> ls-files src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.cpp`. If the file is tracked, the app's reporting path has landed on `jusprin-dev` and app findings can use it. If it is not, that work is still uncommitted in another session's worktree: do not copy, merge or rebuild it. In that case do the server findings first (3 to 7 on the server side, then 20, 25, 26, 27), and tell Kenneth plainly that the app findings wait until that work is committed. The server's own reporting already exists (its Sentry project), so server findings do not wait on anything.

For each finding:
1. Read it and find the code as it is now. Say if it no longer applies, or is already covered by the uncommitted work listed in the background.
2. Reproduce it before changing anything: Kenneth's rule is never to fix a bug you cannot reproduce. For the server, a test against the local stack that shows the wrong outcome counts when it drives the real view with a real provider-shaped answer. For the app, show it in a scratch copy of a build (own `--datadir` and HOME; see `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`, `tests/shell`, `tests/printer_hosts/README.md`), or with the GUI-free bridge tests in `tests/agent` where the failure lives entirely in the host. If you cannot reproduce it, do not fix it; list it with what you tried.
3. Fix it by the rules: for an unexpected error, remove the code at the site so the failure travels up to the top handler with the other side's status, request id and error text kept; for an expected one, use the confirmed table entry and normal control flow, with a test and a count. Build the two expected-errors tables in code from Kenneth's confirmed entries, quoting his words in the eventual commit message. Do not invent an entry or a sentence: where a finding needs a new cause or new wording, stop that finding and put the exact question to Kenneth.
4. Show the fix: the same reproduction now gives the right outcome. For the incident shape (findings 3, 4, 5, 6), show end to end that a provider's 400 is no longer shown or recorded as something else and that a person at the company would hear about it.

Order and stopping points: findings 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 first, since they are the shape of the 2026-11-14 incident. End your first turn when that group is done and shown, with a report and the list of what is left; carry on with the rest when told to.

Rules for this task:
- No stand-ins: a piece is either built and shown working, or named as not built with the reason. If one blocker stops a piece, ask Kenneth the one question, in full, as a question.
- Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` first, and `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Follow `AGENTS.md` on translations for any string added or removed.
- Shared Mac: read "Building on a shared machine" in `AGENTS.md`; check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, build with `-j4`, one build per build directory, decide the target list before starting, reuse the existing dependencies (see the worktree build notes in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md`).
- Server: one local stack only (never a second container, port or database). Run tests with `docker compose exec -T web python manage.py test jusprin --noinput`. Start from what is on disk in that checkout, including the uncommitted `app_errors.py`; do not revert other people's uncommitted changes there, and never stage the `obico-server` submodule.
- Never drive Kenneth's own running JusPrin. Send no email to made-up addresses. Send nothing to the real Sentry projects from tests. Never print or write a secret (Sentry token or DSN, API keys).
- Do not push, and do not land anything on `jusprin-dev` or `master`. Ask Kenneth before committing. Working notes stay untracked and are never added to `.gitignore`.
- Use `gcloud`/`kubectl` only if a finding truly needs production data, and then only with the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

Done looks like: for every finding, one of "fixed and shown", "already covered, by what", "could not reproduce, with what was tried", or "waits on Kenneth, with the question". Your report is for someone who has not seen this work: what a person now sees in each case, what was tested and the result, what is not built, and what is uncommitted where.

JusPrin 2: take the desktop app's error reports and pass them to Sentry

POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports takes a report of an unexpected error
from the JusPrin desktop app and passes it on to the app's own Sentry
project. The app sends one only when the person pressed "Report to JusPrin
team" or turned automatic reports on. A report is anonymous: no token is
read, and the body holds five text fields (app, os, doing, error, where).

The Sentry project's DSN comes from JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN, apart from
the server's own SENTRY_DSN. The report is sent to Sentry before the app is
answered, so the app hears "reported" only once Sentry has it. A server
without the DSN, or a Sentry that refuses the report, fails the request.

A body the app could not have sent (not JSON, over 64 KiB, wrong or missing
fields) also fails the request instead of being answered 400 or 413: our
own app is the only sender, so by the error-handling rules that is an
unexpected error, and the server's own Sentry hears about it. Kenneth,
2026-11-15: "remove the try/catch and make those two checks raise". The
address needs no sign-in, so junk posted to it will show up there too.

Nothing sends to this address until the app's side is released, and no
deployment sets the DSN yet.

Tested: docker compose exec -T web python manage.py test jusprin (288 pass).
EOF
