git apply --cached $S/fix4-A.patch && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
A sign-in or API key that could not be saved says so

With the settings file unwritable, signing in showed "Signed in as …" and
adding a key showed "Key saved on this computer", and both were gone after
quitting. The save step wrote the settings and then answered "saved"
without looking at whether the write worked, so the warnings the app
already has for this were never sent.

The save step now answers from the settings themselves: a write that failed
leaves them unsaved. Preferences then shows "This sign-in could not be
saved, so you will have to sign in again next time JusPrin starts." and,
for a key, its own two lines saying the key works now but could not be
saved.

Not changed: the welcome screen and Home still show no warning for a
sign-in that could not be saved. The app now sends it, but those screens
have no place that draws it.

Tested in a scratch copy of the app with the settings file unwritable, old
build beside this one: the old build showed no warning for the sign-in or
the key; this one shows both, and both are gone after quitting as warned.
EOF
git apply --cached $S/fix4-B.patch && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
An attachment the chat refused no longer stops the project saving

Attaching a file the chat does not take (a .bin), one over the size limit,
or one the project's folder would not take left the project unable to
save: the window title read "Couldn't save" and a save failed every two
seconds until the person pressed Remove on the chip.

The refused attachment's record still named a file in the project's
folder, though none was kept. Saving checks that every file an attachment
names is there, so every save failed. A refused attachment now names no
file; one that is stored names it as before.

Tested: the new bridge test failed on the old code for all three cases
(unsupported type, bytes the page could not hand over, a folder that
refuses the write) and passes now. In a scratch copy of the app, old build
beside this one, for a .bin, a 34 MB picture and a read-only attachments
folder: the old build showed "Couldn't save" with 7 failed saves in 16
seconds each time; this one shows the same chip, "Saved" and no failed
save. A normal attachment still stores, saves and comes back after
reopening the project.
EOF
git apply --cached $S/fix4-C.patch && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Deleting the account waits for a reply running in the main window

Delete account in Preferences sent the request while a reply was still
running in the main window's chat, and the app signed out in the middle of
that reply. The check that makes one wait for the other only looked at the
Preferences window's own host, which has no chat.

The Preferences window's host now asks the docked panel's host whether a
reply is running, and the server is not asked until it has ended.

Not changed: the sentence shown on that refusal is the existing "The
account couldn't be deleted. Check your internet connection, then try
again.", which is wrong for this cause; its wording is still to be
decided. A reply running in a printer or filament chat is not looked at.

Tested: the bridge test for deleting the account now covers a reply
running elsewhere. In a scratch copy of the app, old build beside this
one: the old build's delete request reached the server 9 seconds into the
reply; with this one no request reached the server during the reply, the
account stayed signed in, and Delete went through once the reply had
ended.
EOF
git apply --cached $S/fix4-D.patch && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
A chat whose account or key is gone still shows the model it ran on

A chat that ran on the JusPrin account showed "gpt-5.4-mini" in its greyed
model picker after signing out with an OpenAI key still set up, and a chat
that ran on OpenAI showed "claude-opus-5-5" after its key was removed: the
default of whatever provider was left, a model the chat never used. The
chat itself stays on its provider and says so above the composer.

The app now sends the page the model the chat ran on, with the provider's
name, since the page's model list no longer has that provider. The picker
reads "JusPrin" for an account chat (its model ids are aliases) and the
model's own id for any other provider. A chat nobody has talked in yet
still takes the default.

Tested: the bridge tests and the picker's page test failed on the old code
and pass now. In a scratch copy of the app, old build beside this one: the
account chat's picker read "gpt-5.4-mini" before and "JusPrin" now; the
OpenAI chat's read "claude-opus-5-5" before and "gpt-5.4-mini", the model
it ran on, now. A new chat's picker is unchanged in all three states.
EOF

The server work and the four bug fixes are committed, and the report dialog work is being committed by the session that wrote it. Nothing is pushed. Below are the four open points, each as a decision.

## Where the commits are

- **Server:** `cc677827c6` on `master` in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`. It holds the address that takes the app's error reports. All 288 JusPrin server tests passed before the commit.
- **JusPrin:** the feature branch is `unexpected-error-reports`, in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fix-four-refusal-bugs`. It has four commits so far, one per bug fix.
- **Report dialog:** I asked its session to commit on its own branch. When it has, I will add those commits to the feature branch, resolve the overlaps, then build and test the result.
- **Not committed:** the rules text in `AGENTS.md` and the server's `CLAUDE.md`. You did not name them, so I left them out.

## The four decisions

**Decision needed: what happens after an exception in a native event.** A native event is a click, a menu choice or a timer in the C++ part of the app. In OrcaSlicer today, an exception there is logged, an "OrcaSlicer got an unhandled exception" box is queued, and the exception is thrown again. My reading of the code is that this ends the app; I have not run it. With the new work, the report dialog opens and the app keeps running. Running out of memory still ends it.
- **Keep it running (my pick).** The person keeps their session. The cost is that one action stopped halfway, so the app can be left in an odd state.
- **Stop as before.** Nothing runs in an odd state. The cost is that the dialog cannot show in an app that is ending, so reporting would need extra work at the next start.

**Decision needed: the dialog's promise about project names.** The dialog says the report has "no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or email address." An error's text can quote a file name, and a file name often contains the project's name.
- **Drop "no project names" (my pick).** The sentence stays true. It costs one changed sentence and its 22 translations.
- **Keep the promise and accept the risk.**

Should the dialog drop those words?

**Decision needed: a message left with no reply.** This is the printer chat receiving a message before its page has finished setting up. It should never happen, and the session could only trigger it by breaking the page on purpose. Before, the person saw "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment." with Retry. Now the dialog opens, and their message stays in the chat with nothing under it. They can type again.
- **Leave it (my pick).** No code is written for a fault nobody understands.
- **Mark the message as failed in the chat**, with the same generic line and Retry. This adds handling at the site, which the rules argue against.

Should it stay as it is?

**Decision needed: a failure that repeats.** While a dialog is open, the same failure is not queued twice. Once the person answers, the next occurrence opens the dialog again. With automatic reports on, every occurrence is sent, and the server has no limit.
- **Once per run (my pick).** The same failure opens the dialog once and is sent once, until the app restarts. The cost is that we cannot see how often it repeated within one run.
- **Leave it.** Every repeat is counted. A failure on a timer would then nag the person, or send a report every second.

Should the same failure be reported only once per run?
